project_name: Partly Cloudy Consulting small-scale data center request
aliases: Bethel Road small-scale data center inquiry
status_detail: County minutes show Partly Cloudy Consulting asked Halifax County to consider allowing small-scale data centers in A-1 agricultural zoning for a Bethel Road-area parcel; staff emphasized it was not an application, and the Board voted 8-0 on February 3, 2025 to deny the zoning-amendment request.
notes: County site and IDA site were checked. Separate 2026 ordinance discussions concern data center/BESS policy and potential revenue, not a confirmed new project. Hitachi's Halifax transformer plant supports data center supply chains but is not itself a data center.

status_detail: No operating data center or active Hampton data center proposal found; city is studying future policy and toured Richmond-area facilities.
notes: Hampton official public notice confirms an April 9, 2026 special meeting/tour of two data center facilities. News coverage says Hampton hired a research firm for zoning/policy work and communications staff said there were no operating data centers or active proposals.

status_detail: Tract lists the Hanover site as owned and in development: 1,211 acres along the I-95 corridor near Ashland, zoned for by-right data center use, with up to 2,400 MW across eight substations.
notes: County EDA actively markets data centers and Hanover's county site has launched a data center ordinance/policy process. This is distinct from Tract's rejected Mountain Road proposal.

status_detail: Hanover supervisors voted 4-3 in late May 2026 to reject Tract's proposed roughly 427-430 acre Mountain Road Technology Park data center campus near Mountain Road/Route 33; reporting described 900 MW power demand and phased buildout into the 2030s.
notes: Included because rejected projects count. VPM and Virginia Business both report Board denial, water/power concerns, and Tract as developer.

developer: Harris and Douglas Properties LLC / TradePort Ashland Land LLC
status_detail: Hanover eTRAKiT project REZ2022-00008 is marked DENIED with attachments for Iron Horse data center plans. Project materials described a roughly 200-acre, 13-building, 3.2 million square foot data center campus near Patrick Henry Road/Mount Hermon Road; first building had been modeled for 2026 if approved.
notes: County permitting portal lists the rezoning status as DENIED and includes concept plans, fiscal analysis, TIA, proffers, and staff packets.

status_detail: HHHunt proposed a 400+ acre, 10-building data center campus near the Wyndham community/Ashland Road; Hanover Planning Commission voted against recommendation and the developer withdrew the application in January 2026.
notes: Hanover's official Board Brief states the proposed 400-acre data center on Ashland Road was withdrawn after Planning Commission denial; capacity comes from industry coverage and should be treated as secondary.

status_detail: Carter Funds portfolio page identifies an Enterprise Data Center in Harrisonburg, VA with a Fortune 20 tenant, investment-grade tenancy, and disaster-recovery function backing up a Richmond data center location.
notes: Harrisonburg official site and economic development page were checked. City adopted a data center zoning/SUP ordinance effective January 28, 2025; no separate new city proposal was found beyond the existing Carter/Aphorio enterprise facility.

status_detail: VEDP case study says Meta announced in October 2017 a 970,000-square-foot data center in White Oak Technology Park in Henrico County with a $750 million commitment; later project references describe the multi-phase campus as completed/operational.
notes: County/EDA pages and VEDP were checked. White Oak Technology Park is the main Henrico data center cluster.

status_detail: QTS lists its Richmond 1 campus in Sandston as a 207-acre campus with 238 MW and six facilities. Federal FAST-41 materials for QTS RIC5 in White Oak Technology Park say four of sixteen buildings have been constructed and are operational, with additional RIC5 DC4-DC6 buildings proposed/under permitting for AI workloads.
notes: Capacity is for QTS Richmond 1 from QTS' own site; RIC5 expansion details are from the federal permitting dashboard and indicate mixed operational/construction/development status.

project_name: Iron Mountain Richmond data center campus
status_detail: Iron Mountain describes a 66-acre Richmond campus at White Oak Technology Park in Henrico County with RCH-1 through RCH-4, well over 1 million square feet, and over 200 MW of power capacity; RCH-1/RCH-2 phased capacity is expected in 2028-2029 per Iron Mountain resource pages.
notes: Official Iron Mountain pages give the campus, phase names, location and capacity. Local reporting cites Henrico EDA comments and roughly $1B investment.

project_name: DC BLOX Richmond / Azalea Flea Market data center
status_detail: Local reporting says DC BLOX filed development plans for a 65,000-square-foot data center on roughly 5 acres of the former Azalea Flea Market property after acquiring the larger 30-acre site; industry trackers identify about 10 MW at 5209 Wilkinson Road.
notes: Included under broad project capture; capacity is from tracker, while local news verifies site, developer, and filed plans.

project_name: Darbytown Road / Varina data center proposal
aliases: Centra Development Darbytown Road data center
status_detail: Centra/Wagner sought to build a large data center/industrial project near Darbytown Road and Laburnum Avenue in eastern Henrico; Henrico officials determined the developer lacked vested by-right development rights, the BZA upheld that decision in February 2026, and reporting says the earlier 195-acre data center plan was dropped/pivoted after resistance.
notes: Official BZA minutes and local reporting support a rejected/blocked status; naming varies among Centra Development, Centra Logistics, and Wagner Urban Logistics in coverage.

status_detail: No Henry County data center project, prospect, permit, or named developer found; 2026 local hearings were about possible zoning rules only.
notes: County official site/agenda center checked. WSET quoted county leaders saying there were currently no plans or prospects for data centers in Henry County.

status_detail: No Highland County data center project found in official county/EDA search, local economic development pages, or broader news search.
notes: Official county site was reachable in search results but direct fetch returned 403; Chamber/EDA page and broader web/news searches showed small-business EDA activity but no data center/server farm/hyperscale project.

project_name: Green Plains ethanol plant data center conversion
aliases: Hopewell former ethanol plant data center
status_detail: Volterra Advisors, the city and property owner conducted a case study for converting the vacant former Green Plains ethanol plant at 701 S 6th Ave into a small data center; public reports describe a 50,000-70,000 square foot, roughly 20 MW facility concept.
notes: City official homepage was checked; no city permit/approval located. Treat as early feasibility/planned concept rather than approved construction.

status_detail: No Isle of Wight County data center project, permit, abatement, or named developer found; county appears to be discussing zoning/preemptive regulation only.
notes: Official county, planning/zoning, permits, and WebLink minutes searches were checked. Local social/news snippets indicate draft zoning discussions around data centers, but no formal project was identified.

status_detail: James City County planning case list from June 2010 identifies Cox Communications' Lightfoot Data Center at 6489 Richmond Road and a site-plan request to install upgraded backup generators, indicating an existing operational telecom/data center facility.
notes: James City County also adopted data center policy/zoning controls in 2025; WHRO reported no formal proposals at that time. A separate James City County data-center power equipment manufacturer announcement was excluded because it is manufacturing, not a data center.
